title: MILO Marathon 2026 General Santos Leg Review: What the 2024 Race Was Like
seo_title: MILO Marathon General Santos Review: Cut-offs, Times, Weather
meta_description: National MILO Marathon General Santos leg review from 10 November 2024: a 2:30 half-marathon cut-off, a 2:09 median, 24°C and 91% humidity at the 4.30am start.
dek: What the 10 November 2024 General Santos leg of the National MILO Marathon was like: the pre-dawn starts, the tight MILO cut-offs, the weather, and how fast the half-marathon and 10 km fields ran.
verdict: Enter if you can run a half marathon inside 2 hours 30 and want a well-drilled national-series race with a qualifying place at stake. The 2024 General Santos leg timed 418 half-marathon and 557 10 km finishers, and the field is quicker than most Philippine provincial races: the median half took 2:09, and nine in ten finished inside 2:30. The MILO rules are strict, with a 2.5-hour half-marathon cut-off, a 10 km checkpoint at 1 hour 30 and disqualification for missing either. The 4.30am start was 24°C with 91% humidity, but it was 27°C by 7am.

sections.heading: The Race: Pre-dawn Starts and MILO Rules
paragraphs: The General Santos leg is one of the regional qualifying races of the National MILO Marathon, organised by RUNRIO. The 2024 race ran on Sunday 10 November 2024 [1]. Its timed results cover a half marathon and a 10 km [2], with shorter fun-run distances alongside.

Under the 2024 rules the half marathon set off at 4.30am and the 10 km at 5am [1]. Winners are decided on gun time, and a runner who starts more than 10 minutes after their flag-off is disqualified [1].

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild Start, Fast Warm-up
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's historical record for General Santos City shows 24.1°C at 4am and 23.9°C at 5am on race day, with a dew point of about 22.5°C, 91% humidity and a light breeze [3]. Then the sun did its work: 24.3°C at 6am, 27.1°C at 7am and 28.7°C at 8am [3]. General Santos airport, whose first observation of the day is at 8am, recorded 29°C and 70% humidity then [4].
A half marathoner finishing in the median 2:09 crossed the line around 6.40am, before the worst of it. The slowest finishers, out until after 7am, ran their last kilometres at 27°C in sunshine.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Finisher Items
paragraphs: The MILO cut-offs are tight and enforced. The half marathon closes after 2 hours 30 and the 10 km after 1 hour 30, both counted from when the last runner crosses the start line. Half marathoners must also reach 10 km within 1 hour 30; anyone who misses a limit has to board the official vehicle and is disqualified [1].

In 2024, 44 of the 418 timed half-marathon finishers, about 10.5%, took longer than 2:30, and 54 of the 557 10 km finishers, about 9.7%, took longer than 1:30 [2]. Every half-marathon finisher gets a loot bag and finisher's shirt, but the medal and certificate go only to those inside the cut-off; 10 km runners get a medal only inside the cut-off [1].
The half marathon is for runners 18 and over and needs a Fit-To-Run medical certificate signed by a doctor within two months of race day; the 10 km is for 16 and over [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: For a provincial race the half-marathon field is quick and compact. The median finisher ran 2:09:26, 35.9% broke 2 hours and 89.5% broke 2:30; the slowest 10% took 2:30:36 or longer [2]. The top ten ran from 1:12:37 to 1:31:27, and the fastest woman ran 1:34:13 [2]. Women were only 17.7% of half-marathon finishers [2].

The 10 km is more mixed: a median of 1:14:06, 12.6% under an hour, a top ten from 33:28 to 45:09, and an even split between men and women [2]. The top male and female finishers of each qualifying leg are eligible for an all-expenses trip to the National Finals, held in Cagayan de Oro in 2024 [1].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race kits are claimed in person, with the schedule and venue announced at least two weeks before the race. There is a baggage area for the 10 km and half marathon only, and the official MILO singlet and race number must be worn [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next General Santos Leg?
paragraphs: Yes, if you can comfortably run a half marathon in under 2 hours 30 and reach 10 km inside 1 hour 30. The early start and compact field make it a good race for a solid time, and a podium place carries a National Finals spot.
Think twice if you are a newer runner or walker: about one half-marathon finisher in ten in 2024 came in after the cut-off and missed the medal. The 10 km, with a median of 1:14, is the safer choice.
The 2026 MILO calendar put the General Santos leg on 9 August 2026 [5]. Check the next leg's date, start times and cut-offs on the MILO entry page before booking.
This review draws on the 2024 race rules, the official results, and historical weather records for General Santos City.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the MILO Marathon General Santos leg?
faqs.answer: Tight. Under the 2024 rules the half marathon closes after 2 hours 30, with 10 km to be reached in 1 hour 30, and the 10 km closes after 1 hour 30, all counted from when the last runner crosses the start. Runners who miss a limit are disqualified. In 2024 about 10% of timed finishers in each race came in after the cut-off.

faqs.question: How fast is the half marathon at the MILO General Santos leg?
faqs.answer: Quick for a provincial race. In November 2024 the median half marathoner finished in 2:09:26, 35.9% broke 2 hours and 89.5% broke 2:30. The top ten ran from 1:12:37 to 1:31:27, and the fastest woman ran 1:34:13. Only 17.7% of half-marathon finishers were women. The 2026 leg was scheduled for 9 August.

faqs.question: How hot is the MILO Marathon in General Santos?
faqs.answer: Mild at the start, warm soon after. On race morning in November 2024 General Santos City was about 24°C with 91% humidity and a light breeze at the 4.30am half-marathon start. It reached 27°C by 7am and 29°C by 8am, so the slowest half marathoners finished in rising heat and sunshine.
